quiz.question_id: Pada loop yang meluncurkan goroutine anonim, mengapa contoh memakai `i := i` sebelum `go func()`?
quiz.question_en: In the loop that launches anonymous goroutines, why does the example use `i := i` before `go func()`?
options_id: Agar setiap goroutine menangkap salinan nilai `i` untuk iterasi itu
Agar `i` menjadi variabel global yang dipakai semua goroutine
Agar semua goroutine otomatis berjalan parallel
Agar loop berhenti setelah satu iterasi
options_en: So each goroutine captures its own copy of `i` for that iteration
So `i` becomes a global variable shared by all goroutines
So all goroutines automatically run in parallel
So the loop stops after one iteration

quiz.question_id: Pernyataan mana yang paling tepat membedakan concurrency dan parallelism di Go?
quiz.question_en: Which statement best distinguishes concurrency from parallelism in Go?
options_id: Concurrency dan parallelism adalah istilah yang sama
Concurrency berarti task overlap dalam waktu, sedangkan parallelism berarti benar-benar berjalan serentak di core berbeda
Parallelism selalu terjadi setiap kali ada dua goroutine
Concurrency hanya mungkin jika `GOMAXPROCS` lebih dari 1
options_en: Concurrency and parallelism are the same thing
Concurrency means tasks overlap in time, while parallelism means they truly run simultaneously on different cores
Parallelism always happens whenever there are two goroutines
Concurrency is only possible if `GOMAXPROCS` is greater than 1

quiz.question_id: Jika `runtime.GOMAXPROCS(1)` dipakai, kondisi mana yang masih mungkin?
quiz.question_en: If `runtime.GOMAXPROCS(1)` is used, which situation is still possible?
options_id: Dua goroutine tidak bisa berjalan sama sekali
Dua goroutine tetap bisa concurrent, tetapi tidak parallel di dua core berbeda
Setiap goroutine otomatis menjadi satu OS thread
Keyword `go` menjadi tidak valid
options_en: Two goroutines cannot run at all
Two goroutines can still be concurrent, but not parallel on two different cores
Each goroutine automatically becomes one OS thread
The `go` keyword becomes invalid

quiz.question_id: Pada potongan `go func() { ... }()`, apa arti pasangan `go` dan `()` itu?
quiz.question_en: In the snippet `go func() { ... }()`, what do the `go` and `()` together mean?
options_id: Function literal didefinisikan tetapi tidak pernah dipanggil
Function literal dipanggil nanti ketika `main()` selesai
Function literal langsung dipanggil sebagai goroutine baru
`()` hanya diperlukan agar fungsi menjadi exported
options_en: The function literal is defined but never called
The function literal is called later when `main()` exits
The function literal is invoked immediately as a new goroutine
The `()` is only needed to make the function exported

quiz.question_id: Mengapa `time.Sleep` disebut cara yang buruk untuk menunggu goroutine selesai?
quiz.question_en: Why is `time.Sleep` described as a poor way to wait for goroutines to finish?
options_id: Karena hanya bekerja untuk buffered channel
Karena durasinya hanya tebakan, bukan sinkronisasi deterministik terhadap pekerjaan yang benar-benar selesai
Karena `Sleep` selalu menghentikan semua goroutine lain
Karena `Sleep` membuat program menjadi single-threaded
options_en: Because it only works for buffered channels
Because the duration is only a guess, not deterministic synchronization with actual completion
Because `Sleep` always stops all other goroutines
Because `Sleep` makes the program single-threaded

quiz.question_id: Berapa orde memori awal yang disebutkan untuk satu goroutine?
quiz.question_en: What starting memory size does the lesson mention for a goroutine?
options_id: Sekitar 2KB
Sekitar 1MB
Sekitar 8MB seperti OS thread
Tidak membutuhkan memori sama sekali
options_en: About 2KB
About 1MB
About 8MB like an OS thread
It needs no memory at all

quiz.question_id: Jika variabel loop tidak dicapture dengan benar pada goroutine anonim, gejala apa yang paling mungkin muncul?
quiz.question_en: If the loop variable is not captured correctly in an anonymous goroutine, what symptom is most likely?
options_id: Setiap goroutine pasti mencetak 0,1,2,3,4 secara stabil
Banyak goroutine bisa mencetak nilai `i` yang sama atau nilai yang tidak sesuai iterasinya
Program otomatis panic ketika loop selesai
Compiler otomatis membekukan nilai `i` tanpa bantuan apa pun
options_en: Every goroutine will reliably print 0,1,2,3,4
Many goroutines may print the same `i` value or a value that does not match their intended iteration
The program automatically panics when the loop ends
The compiler automatically freezes the value of `i` without any help

quiz.question_id: Apa implikasi terpenting dari fakta bahwa `main()` berjalan di main goroutine?
quiz.question_en: What is the most important implication of the fact that `main()` runs in the main goroutine?
options_id: Goroutine lain otomatis di-wait saat `main()` return
Semua goroutine lain dihentikan ketika `main()` selesai
Semua goroutine lain menjadi child process OS
Keyword `go` hanya boleh dipakai di `main()`
options_en: Other goroutines are automatically waited for when `main()` returns
All other goroutines are terminated when `main()` finishes
All other goroutines become OS child processes
The `go` keyword may only be used in `main()`

quiz.question_id: Potongan mana yang benar untuk meluncurkan fungsi `say` secara concurrent?
quiz.question_en: Which snippet correctly launches the `say` function concurrently?
options_id: `say go("hello")`
`concurrent say("hello")`
`go say("hello")`
`async say("hello")`
options_en: `say go("hello")`
`concurrent say("hello")`
`go say("hello")`
`async say("hello")`

quiz.question_id: Mengapa Go dapat menjalankan ribuan goroutine lebih mudah daripada ribuan OS thread?
quiz.question_en: Why can Go run thousands of goroutines more easily than thousands of OS threads?
options_id: Karena goroutine tidak memerlukan scheduler
Karena goroutine tidak memiliki stack
Karena goroutine dikelola runtime Go dengan overhead awal yang kecil
Karena goroutine selalu berjalan serial
options_en: Because goroutines do not need a scheduler
Because goroutines do not have stacks
Because goroutines are managed by the Go runtime with small starting overhead
Because goroutines always run serially
